title: The form that delivered one lead twice
blurb: Fresh idempotency keys and raw HTML in fields.
prompt: A marketing CRM received duplicate leads after webhook retries produced new keys, and a stored HTML field rendered as script on the admin dashboard. The captcha token was also replayable. Review it, fix it, and prove delivery is keyed and inputs are inert.
aiNote: The draft retries each handler under a fresh idempotency key, so downstream systems create duplicate records, and it stores raw markup that the admin UI renders, turning a public form into a stored-XSS vector; captcha consumption is non-atomic.
testIdea: Replay a submission and assert the handler is invoked once per key; submit script markup and assert it renders inert in the admin view; race two captcha replays and assert one is rejected.
followUps: Which fields must be redacted by default in exports?
How do you version a form without breaking in-flight sessions?
What detection stops a slow botnet sweep?
